findings.title: Non-SDK-style project file
findings.message: Project 'Woodgrove.Domain' uses the legacy non-SDK project format.
findings.remediation: Convert the project to the SDK style (<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">). Replace TargetFrameworkVersion with a TargetFramework moniker, move packages.config entries to PackageReference, and let the SDK glob source files instead of listing them. Do this before other migration work: nearly every later step assumes an SDK-style project.

findings.title: packages.config instead of PackageReference
findings.message: Project 'Woodgrove.Domain' declares NuGet dependencies in packages.config rather than PackageReference.
findings.remediation: Migrate packages.config to PackageReference (Visual Studio offers an in-place migration, or run 'dotnet migrate'-style tooling). PackageReference is required for SDK-style projects and gives transitive restore.

findings.title: System.Web dependency outside WebForms
findings.message: Project 'Woodgrove.Domain' references System.Web outside of WebForms. System.Web is not available on modern .NET; the dependent code needs replacing.
findings.remediation: System.Web is not available on modern .NET. Replace the dependent code: HttpContext usage moves to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http, HttpUtility to System.Web.HttpUtility's modern equivalents or System.Net.WebUtility.

findings.title: BinaryFormatter
findings.message: Uses BinaryFormatter, which is removed in .NET 9 and throws when used. Replace it with a safe serializer such as System.Text.Json, MessagePack, or protobuf.
findings.remediation: BinaryFormatter is removed in .NET 9 and throws when invoked (it was also a well-known security risk). Replace it with a safe serializer: System.Text.Json, MessagePack, or protobuf. Changing serialization format may require a data migration.

findings.title: System.Data.SqlClient
findings.message: Uses System.Data.SqlClient, which is in maintenance mode. Switch to Microsoft.Data.SqlClient (note its Encrypt=true default change, see MIG7002).
findings.remediation: System.Data.SqlClient is in maintenance mode. Switch to Microsoft.Data.SqlClient, and review the Encrypt=true default change in 4.0+ that can break existing connection strings (see MIG7002).

findings.title: COM reference or interop assembly
findings.message: Project 'Woodgrove.Interop' has a COM reference ('FabrikamImagingLib'). COM interop works on modern .NET only when targeting Windows (net-windows); it is a Windows lock-in and unavailable elsewhere.
findings.remediation: COM interop is supported on modern .NET only when targeting Windows (net-windows), so regenerate the interop assembly there. It is a Windows lock-in: if the app must run cross-platform there is no COM support off Windows, so the component must be replaced. Very old or ActiveX components may also need updating even on Windows.

findings.title: Vendored DLL with no source and no NuGet equivalent
findings.message: Project 'Woodgrove.Interop' references a vendored assembly ('Litware.ChequeScanner') from a checked-in path, not a NuGet package. Confirm it runs on modern .NET, since many such assemblies are Framework-only or ActiveX/COM with no supported successor.
findings.remediation: A third-party assembly referenced from a checked-in path rather than a NuGet package. Assess it per assembly: confirm it loads on modern .NET (many Framework-only or ActiveX/COM assemblies do not), find a supported successor or NuGet package, or plan a replacement. If the vendor is defunct and there is no equivalent, this can block the migration.

findings.title: Windows Registry access
findings.message: Accesses the Windows Registry (Microsoft.Win32.Registry). The registry does not exist on non-Windows platforms; the call throws PlatformNotSupportedException there.
findings.remediation: The Windows Registry does not exist on other platforms; Microsoft.Win32.Registry throws PlatformNotSupportedException there. Move configuration/state to a cross-platform store (config files, environment variables, a database).

findings.title: System.Management / WMI
findings.message: Uses WMI (System.Management). On modern .NET this is Windows-only (via the System.Management package) and throws PlatformNotSupportedException elsewhere.
findings.remediation: WMI (System.Management) is Windows-only on modern .NET and throws PlatformNotSupportedException elsewhere. If the app must run cross-platform, replace WMI queries with platform-appropriate APIs.

findings.title: P/Invoke to a Windows system DLL
findings.message: P/Invokes the Windows system library 'kernel32.dll' via [DllImport]. This works on modern .NET only when targeting Windows (net-windows); it is a Windows lock-in and won't run cross-platform.
findings.remediation: P/Invoke to a Windows system library (kernel32/user32/advapi32/...) works on modern .NET when targeting Windows (net-windows). It is a Windows lock-in: for cross-platform, guard the call with OperatingSystem.IsWindows() and provide a non-Windows path, or replace it with a cross-platform .NET API.

findings.title: GAC reference (no HintPath)
findings.message: Assembly 'Litware.Web.Controls' is referenced from the GAC (strong-named, no HintPath). The GAC does not exist on modern .NET.
findings.remediation: Replace the GAC reference with a NuGet package or an explicit HintPath to a checked-in assembly. The Global Assembly Cache does not exist on modern .NET, so GAC-resolved dependencies will not load.

findings.title: Package has no version supporting the target framework
findings.message: Package 'Microsoft.AspNet.Mvc' has no version that supports net10.0. ASP.NET MVC 5 runs only on .NET Framework. Consider: ASP.NET Core MVC.
findings.remediation: Replace the package with a version or successor that targets modern .NET, or remove the dependency. See the suggested replacement in the finding message.

findings.title: Package has no version supporting the target framework
findings.message: Package 'Microsoft.AspNet.Web.Optimization' has no version that supports net10.0. System.Web bundling/minification runs only on .NET Framework. Consider: A build-time bundler or ASP.NET Core static asset pipeline.
findings.remediation: Replace the package with a version or successor that targets modern .NET, or remove the dependency. See the suggested replacement in the finding message.

findings.title: ASP.NET WebForms
findings.message: Project 'Woodgrove.Web' is an ASP.NET WebForms application (.aspx/.ascx present). WebForms has no equivalent on modern .NET and needs re-architecting (e.g. to Razor Pages, MVC, or Blazor).
findings.remediation: WebForms has no counterpart on modern .NET. Plan a re-architecture to Razor Pages, MVC, or Blazor. This is an architectural decision, not a mechanical port.

findings.title: ConfigurationManager.AppSettings usage
findings.message: Reads configuration via ConfigurationManager.AppSettings. On modern .NET this requires the System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager package, or migration to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.
findings.remediation: On modern .NET, either add the System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager package to keep reading app.config, or migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration (appsettings.json, environment variables, options pattern).
